passages.provision_quote: An employer shall not rely solely on an ADS when making a discipline, termination, or deactivation decision.
passages.note: Binding state regulation of automated decision systems at work, but its mechanisms are notice, use prohibitions and human review rather than pre-use safety testing or developer liability.

rows.reasoning: SB 7 (2025-2026), which McNerney introduced, imposes mandatory duties on employers deploying automated decision systems: pre-use notice, prohibited uses, a requirement that an employer "shall not rely solely on an ADS when making a discipline, termination, or deactivation decision", and a $500 civil penalty enforced by the Labor Commissioner. That excludes "Suggest AI safety guidelines but let companies choose whether to follow them" and "Impose strict government approval requirements before any AI system can be deployed", but it matches neither remaining rung's object: it requires notice, not "safety testing before AI can be used in high-stakes areas like hiring, healthcare, and policing", and it binds deploying employers rather than holding "AI developers legally responsible when their systems cause harm". The bill establishes the pro-oversight side only.
